I do product demos every day, and my first rule is simple: never leave a silence. In a demo without slides, the customer is looking at your screen, and if you stop talking, they do not know what to look at. So I tell them what I am doing while I do it. Now I'm opening the dashboard. As you can see, the system is checking the invoices. My second rule is to start with their problem, not with my menu. Nobody wants to see every button. And my third rule is to always use a sandbox, never a live system with real data. Things go wrong in demos. If the screen freezes, do not panic. Say it's loading, and while you are waiting, ask the customer a question. A good question is worth more than a perfect screen.

The worst demo I ever saw lasted ninety minutes. The salesperson showed us every menu, every tab and every setting, and he never asked us a single question. By minute twenty, my team was reading their email. The best demo was the opposite. Before the call, the salesperson asked us to send her three real invoices. During the demo, she was processing our own invoices, and she kept telling us what was happening. The system is reading the supplier name. Now it's checking the price against the order. After fifteen minutes, she stopped sharing her screen and asked us one question: is this what your team does today? It was a very short demo, and it was the one we remembered. We signed six weeks later.
